title: Starter and fermentation
summary: Read a starter and a dough by evidence rather than by the clock.
outcomes: Explain the decision this module teaches and the evidence behind it.
startingAssumptions: No kitchen or equipment is required; every scene is fictional.

beats.title: Read the starter, not the timer
beats.outcome: Make a reasoned choice and name the evidence that would change it.
beats.explanation: A recipe time is a prediction. [[hearth-m01-concept|Fermentation readiness]] shows in the starter itself: roughly doubled, bubbly through its depth, with a domed top. Check the evidence and treat the clock as a reminder to look.

handbook.markdown: Record the room temperature beside every reading. Over a few bakes the records turn the recipe's single time into a range you can trust for your own kitchen.

beats.recap: A recipe time is a prediction.

beats.title: Let temperature move the schedule
beats.outcome: Make a reasoned choice and name the evidence that would change it.
beats.explanation: Temperature changes how fast fermentation runs. A cooler kitchen delays the peak and a warmer one brings it forward. Move the schedule to match the evidence rather than forcing the dough to match the schedule.

handbook.markdown: When the dough runs late, extend the step that can stretch. A cold proof usually can; mixing an under-ripe starter usually cannot be undone.

beats.recap: Temperature changes how fast fermentation runs.

recap.title: Starter and fermentation: what to keep
recap.markdown: Read the evidence the loaf gives you, change one thing at a time and write down what you saw.

appliedTask.title: Apply it to your next bake
appliedTask.prompt: Describe one decision from this module you will make differently next time, and the evidence you will check.
appliedTask.modelAnswer: Name the decision, the evidence that justifies it and the result that would make you change course.
appliedTask.reasoning: A transferable answer ties a decision to observable evidence rather than to a fixed time or rule.
